title: Fubini identity: pairing u − u∗φ with a test function equals the φ-average of translation differences
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let S ⊆ ℝⁿ be a measurable set (ℝⁿ = Euclid n with Lebesgue measure), and let φ, u, g : ℝⁿ → ℝ. Assume φ is continuous with compact support and ∫_{ℝⁿ} φ = 1, u is integrable on S, g is continuous with compact support, and g(x) = 0 for every x ∉ S. Then ∫_{ℝⁿ} (u(x) − ∫_S u(y)φ(x − y) dy)·g(x) dx = ∫_{ℝⁿ} φ(z)·(∫_S u(y)(g(y) − g(y + z)) dy) dz.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (S : Set (Euclid n)) (φ u g : Euclid n → ℝ), MeasurableSet S → Continuous φ → HasCompactSupport φ → ∫ y, φ y = 1 → IntegrableOn u S → Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ x, x ∉ S → g x = 0) → ∫ x, (u x - ∫ y in S, u y * φ (x - y)) * g x = ∫ z, φ z * ∫ y in S, u y * (g y - g (y + z))
